purpose: The plan cards at the top of Pricing: a billing-period toggle over a framed row of pricing cards, each with its plan name, its price for the picked period, what it includes and one button. The recommended plan sits on a raised surface and carries a tag. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'pricing-plans', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `registration-frame`, `toggle-group`, `card-grid`, `pricing-card` and `button`; the picked period is local state. The band runs full bleed (the page's inline inset only, closed by a bottom rule) and centres its frame at the site measure, with rules on its sides.
useWhen: Use PricingPlans for price cards with a billing-period toggle on the public pricing page, the plans side by side at the top of Pricing.
avoidWhen: To compare plans or support tiers feature by feature → use `plan-comparison`.
To compare Azion with one competitor → use `competitor-comparison`.
related: pricing-card` — the card each plan renders with.
plan-comparison` — the matrix that sits under these cards.
bestPractices: Give every plan one price per period, matched by `period`; a price without a `period` applies to every period.
Highlight one plan; it is raised and is the only card that shows its tag.
Put terms that hold for every period in the plan's `description`; a price's own `details` replaces it for that period.
Keep `features` to five or so short labels led by an icon.
